text.arabic_uthmani: جَزَآؤُهُمْ عِندَ رَبِّهِمْ جَنَّٰتُ عَدْنٍۢ تَجْرِى مِن تَحْتِهَا ٱلْأَنْهَٰرُ خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَآ أَبَدًۭا ۖ رَّضِىَ ٱللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ وَرَضُوا۟ عَنْهُ ۚ ذَٰلِكَ لِمَنْ خَشِىَ رَبَّهُۥ

words.gloss_range: their recompense, locally selected as positive requital and grammatically equated with the garden reward
words.root_gloss_range: requiting, repaying, compensating, rewarding, or punishing according to context; the local reward frame selects beneficial recompense

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the divine-nearness phrase that frames the recompense
the garden predicate that selects the reward side of recompense

words.prose: {{ar:جَزَآؤُهُمْ}} ({{tr:jazāʾuhum}}) begins the ayah by naming what the prior believing-and-doing group receives, so 98:7's verdict immediately becomes recompense disclosure. The root can cover reward or punishment, but {{ar:عِندَ رَبِّهِمْ}} ({{tr:ʿinda rabbihim}}) and {{ar:جَنَّٰتُ}} ({{tr:jannātu}}) select the positive pole: measured return for action, not an undifferentiated gift. The opening also answers the commanded conduct of 98:5 and contrasts the eternal fire of 98:6 with eternal gardens and reciprocity. The verbless equation makes the recompense itself the gardens, and the rest of the ayah unfolds that package through place, duration, reciprocal satisfaction, and the final fear-of-Lord condition.

topics.headline: prior verdict becomes recompense disclosure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the opening pronoun carries the delimited believers of 98:7 into the reward rather than starting a new audience.
topics.reason: QAC marks the attached plural suffix, and the boundary evidence ties it to the believing group named in 98:7.

topics.headline: neutral requital root selected as reward
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees reward as calibrated return for deeds, while the surrounding paradise language fixes the otherwise neutral recompense root on its beneficial side.
topics.reason: The root range includes both reward and punishment, but local predicate and divine-proximity framing select positive recompense.

topics.headline: recompense is equated with the gardens
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the reward is not merely paid beside the gardens; the nominal sentence identifies the gardens as the recompense.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes {{ar:جَزَآؤُهُمْ}} ({{tr:jazāʾuhum}}) the subject and {{ar:جَنَّٰتُ عَدْنٍ}} ({{tr:jannātu ʿadnin}}) the predicate.

topics.headline: reward field answers the prior command and contrast
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the ayah as a structured answer to prior action and to the opposite eternal destination in 98:6.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows tie the recompense opening to deed language, the garden-river reward field, and the contrast with the fire scene in 98:6.

words.gloss_range: locative-relational nearness, custody, and estimation framing the recompense with their Lord
words.root_gloss_range: nearness, being with or at, possession/custody, and evaluative presence; locally it frames the reward as with their Lord

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the recompense noun located by the adverbial phrase

words.prose: {{ar:عِندَ}} ({{tr:ʿinda}}) interrupts the subject-predicate line before the gardens are named, so divine nearness becomes the frame for the reward. Attachment evidence favors the phrase as locating {{ar:جَزَآؤُهُمْ}} ({{tr:jazāʾuhum}}) with respect to their Lord, while the live garden attachment keeps a secondary pressure: the entire paradise scene is being drawn into God's domain, custody, and judgment.

topics.headline: divine proximity frames the reward before gardens appear
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the reward located in divine nearness before its garden form is disclosed.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence mark {{ar:عِندَ}} ({{tr:ʿinda}}) as an accusative locative adverbial tied to the recompense.

topics.headline: garden attachment remains secondary inside a divine formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the phrase can color both reward and garden scene, but local syntax chiefly makes it the reward's divine-location frame.
topics.reason: The alternate attachment is meaningful, but attachment evidence specifically relates {{ar:عِندَ}} ({{tr:ʿinda}}) to the recompense head.

words.gloss_range: their Lord, a relational divine title governing the reward's location
words.root_gloss_range: lordship, ownership, nurturing, sustaining, governing, and mastership; locally a possessive Lord relation

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the closing singular Lord relation that returns to the opening title

words.prose: {{ar:رَبِّهِمْ}} ({{tr:rabbihim}}) completes the nearness phrase as a possessed Lord relation: the reward is with their Lord, not with an abstract authority. The repeated plural suffix keeps the 98:7 group tight, and the boundary moves from 98:7's created-order ranking into the Lord's presence. The later {{ar:رَبَّهُۥ}} ({{tr:rabbahu}}) makes the same lordship frame return in singular form at the closing condition.

topics.headline: their Lord locates reward in a relational title
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the reward as located with the sustaining Lord already bound to the recipients.
topics.reason: The word is genitive under {{ar:عِندَ}} ({{tr:ʿinda}}) and carries the same plural possessive chain as the opening recompense.

topics.headline: lordship frames both reward and condition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that lordship is not incidental; it frames the promise at the opening and returns as the object of awe at the end.
topics.reason: The same root and title recur at word 23, where the closing condition is directed to {{ar:رَبَّهُۥ}} ({{tr:rabbahu}}).

topics.headline: creation ranking moves to Creator-level location
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees 98:7's created-order ranking move into the presence of the Lord who sustains and evaluates.
topics.reason: The governed phrase mediates between recompense and gardens, and the boundary rows connect the prior creation-scale verdict to this Lord-location.

words.gloss_range: gardens as the nominative reward predicate, plural and formulaically tied to permanence, rivers, and approval
words.root_gloss_range: covering, concealing, protecting, garden enclosure, and related hiddenness; locally the paradise-garden branch is selected

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the Edenic qualifier in the fixed garden phrase

words.prose: {{ar:جَنَّٰتُ}} ({{tr:jannātu}}) completes the nominal equation: their recompense is gardens. Its plural form makes the reward spatially expansive, while the root's covering field lets the garden image feel protected and enclosed rather than merely scenic. The doubled center of the word makes that enclosed density audible. In this ayah the word also joins a fixed paradise ecology with {{ar:عَدْنٍ}} ({{tr:ʿadnin}}), flowing rivers, permanence, and the later approval clause, answering the opposite fire destination in 98:6.

topics.headline: gardens complete the recompense equation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the gardens as the disclosed content of recompense, whether read as predicate or appositive specification.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence identifies {{ar:جَنَّٰتُ عَدْنٍ}} ({{tr:jannātu ʿadnin}}) as the predicate of the opening recompense.

topics.headline: concealment pressure enriches plural gardens
topics.reader_payoff: The reader pictures paradise as multiple protected garden-realms, with covering pressure enriching but not replacing the local garden sense.
topics.reason: The covering branch belongs to the root family, while the local surface and collocation select the garden/paradise noun.

topics.headline: garden ecology answers the fire contrast
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a whole reward ecology, not an isolated image: gardens, fixed abode, flowing rivers, permanence, and approval answer the fire scene of 98:6.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows preserve the fixed {{ar:جَنَّٰتُ عَدْنٍ}} ({{tr:jannātu ʿadnin}}) collocation and the structural contrast with the eternal fire destination in 98:6.

topics.headline: compressed sound suits dense enclosure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can hear the doubled sound as matching the compact, enclosed garden image.
topics.reason: The sound observation is tied to the actual doubled consonant in the local surface form.

words.gloss_range: Edenic permanence as the genitive qualifier of the gardens, lexicalized as a fixed paradise name
words.root_gloss_range: settling, staying, permanent dwelling, and source/deposit imagery; locally lexicalized into the Edenic garden collocation

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the garden head noun qualified by Eden

words.prose: {{ar:عَدْنٍۢ}} ({{tr:ʿadnin}}) is the genitive qualifier that makes the gardens an Edenic abode, not just any garden scene. Its fixed Quranic pairing with {{ar:جَنَّٰتُ}} ({{tr:jannātu}}) keeps the place-name force strong, while the settlement and source imagery gives the reward a sense of deep anchorage. When the next phrase says rivers flow from beneath, that anchorage becomes spatial: permanent abode and productive underside work together. Its tanwīn also links the abode word audibly to the later forever-adverb, so permanence returns as cadence as well as meaning.

topics.headline: Eden qualifies the gardens as a fixed abode
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees permanence built into the garden phrase itself, not added only later by the eternity adverb.
topics.reason: {{ar:عَدْنٍۢ}} ({{tr:ʿadnin}}) is genitive under {{ar:جَنَّٰتُ}} ({{tr:jannātu}}), and the evidence treats the pairing as a fixed paradise formula.

topics.headline: source imagery meets rivers from beneath
topics.reader_payoff: The reader senses the gardens as an enduring source-surface from which the river scene emerges, while the local noun remains the Edenic abode name.
topics.reason: The mineral-source branch supplies image pressure, but QAC marks the local surface as a proper Edenic noun in construct with gardens.

topics.headline: tanwin links abode and forever
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears permanence recur as both place-name and later duration, tying abode to foreverness.
topics.reason: The row ties the local form to the recurring flowing-beneath formula and to the later indefinite duration word.

words.gloss_range: ongoing intransitive flowing that animates the garden description before the rivers are named
words.root_gloss_range: running, flowing, moving along a course, sailing, and cosmic or event motion; locally river-flow in a paradise formula

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the governed underside source phrase after the source preposition
the delayed river subject named after the source phrase

words.prose: {{ar:تَجْرِى}} ({{tr:tajrī}}) shifts the reward from nominal identification into moving landscape. The imperfect Form I presents ongoing intransitive flow, and because the verb precedes its delayed subject, the reader hears movement before the rivers are named. The broader root can describe water, ships, heavenly bodies, and events moving on course, but here that movement vocabulary is locally narrowed to the recognizable garden-river formula. Its light glide and smooth cadence let the continuing flow be felt in sound as well as syntax.

topics.headline: ongoing flow arrives before the rivers
topics.reader_payoff: The reader experiences the reward scene as animated by flow before the rivers are identified.
topics.reason: QAC marks an imperfect verb, and attachment evidence makes {{ar:ٱلْأَنْهَٰرُ}} ({{tr:al-anhāru}}) its delayed subject.

topics.headline: course-movement root narrows to river flow
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears paradisal water as part of a wider Quranic vocabulary of things moving on a course, while the local formula keeps rivers as the selected sense.
topics.reason: The wider root range is real, but the local subject and prepositional source phrase select river-flow rather than ship or cosmic motion.

topics.headline: fixed flowing-beneath formula animates paradise
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes the flow clause as a formulaic paradise marker, not a decorative add-on.
topics.reason: The verb is tied locally to {{ar:مِن تَحْتِهَا ٱلْأَنْهَٰرُ}} ({{tr:min taḥtihā al-anhāru}}), the same dense formula identified by the CRITICAL rows.

topics.headline: smooth sound supports continuous flow
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can hear a light glide that matches the continuing movement named by the verb.
topics.reason: The phonetic observation is anchored in the local surface form and supports the flow image without changing the parse.

words.gloss_range: source preposition turning beneathness into the origin path of the rivers

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the underside phrase governed by the source preposition
the delayed river subject foregrounded after the source phrase

words.prose: {{ar:مِنْ}} ({{tr:min}}) is small but structural: it makes {{ar:تَحْتِهَا}} ({{tr:taḥtihā}}) the source from which the rivers flow. The phrase is therefore not merely rivers located below the gardens, and it is not partitive extraction from the gardens; it foregrounds emergence from beneath before the subject {{ar:ٱلْأَنْهَٰرُ}} ({{tr:al-anhāru}}) appears.

topics.headline: source marker turns beneath into origin
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices emergence from beneath the gardens, not just rivers positioned under them.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes {{ar:تَحْتِهَا}} ({{tr:taḥtihā}}) the complement governed by {{ar:مِنْ}} ({{tr:min}}) as a source path.

topics.headline: particle holds the flowing-beneath formula together
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the formula depend on the particle that joins flow to underside.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL row specifically identifies the recurrent formula as {{ar:تَجْرِى مِن تَحْتِهَا}} ({{tr:tajrī min taḥtihā}}).

words.gloss_range: beneath them, a genitive source-beneath phrase with a feminine suffix referring to the gardens
words.root_gloss_range: under, beneath, lower part, underside, and subordinate position; locally the physical underside-source of the garden formula

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the source preposition governing the underside phrase
the Edenic permanence qualifier that prepares the foundation image

words.prose: {{ar:تَحْتِهَا}} ({{tr:taḥtihā}}) binds the river source to the gardens through the feminine suffix. Governed by {{ar:مِنْ}} ({{tr:min}}), it creates a composite source-beneath marker: the rivers emerge from under the garden realm. The word also turns the garden scene into a surface with a hidden productive foundation, especially after {{ar:عَدْنٍۢ}} ({{tr:ʿadnin}}) has made permanence and anchorage part of the place. Its tight lower-surface sound contrasts with the smoother flow verb.

topics.headline: underneath becomes the rivers' source path
topics.reader_payoff: The reader pictures rivers emerging from beneath the gardens, not merely lying somewhere below them.
topics.reason: The word is genitive under {{ar:مِنْ}} ({{tr:min}}), and attachment evidence marks it as the source path for {{ar:تَجْرِى}} ({{tr:tajrī}}).

topics.headline: suffix locks the underside to the gardens
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the gardens as both visible surface and hidden foundation through the suffix-bound underside.
topics.reason: The feminine suffix refers back to the non-human plural gardens and keeps the garden referent compressed inside the source phrase.

topics.headline: beneathness completes the stable flow formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes {{ar:تَحْتِهَا}} ({{tr:taḥtihā}}) as the spatial operator of the familiar rivers-beneath reward idiom.
topics.reason: The collocation evidence ties the underside term tightly to flow and rivers in the repeated reward formula.

topics.headline: tight sound contrasts with smooth flow
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can hear the compact lower-surface word contrast with the smoother flow verb.
topics.reason: The sound observation remains tied to the local word and its place in the flow phrase.

words.gloss_range: the definite plural rivers, delayed subject of the flow verb and final noun of the paradise formula
words.root_gloss_range: river, channel, flowing water, and daylight/daytime associations; locally the river branch is selected with secondary luminosity pressure
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْأَنْهَٰرُ}} ({{tr:al-anhāru}}) finally names the subject after the reader has already heard the flowing and its source. The definite plural treats the rivers as a known component of paradise discourse and scales the scene to match the plural gardens. The daylight branch in the root family can add luminosity pressure, but the local word remains rivers: channels that complete the flowing-from-beneath formula.

topics.headline: known plural rivers arrive after their flow
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears flow first, then recognizes the familiar plural rivers of the paradise scene.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence make the definite plural noun the delayed subject of {{ar:تَجْرِى}} ({{tr:tajrī}}).

topics.headline: daylight root pressure brightens the river image
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can sense luminous pressure around the rivers, while the local noun remains water channels beneath the gardens.
topics.reason: The daylight branch belongs to the root family, but local grammar and formula select the plural river noun.

topics.headline: rivers complete the garden-flow formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the rivers as structurally necessary to the paradise formula rather than ornamental scenery.
topics.reason: The rows tie {{ar:ٱلْأَنْهَٰرُ}} ({{tr:al-anhāru}}) to gardens, flow, and beneathness in a stable reward phrase.

words.gloss_range: abiding ones, an accusative circumstantial active participle describing the recipients' enduring state
words.root_gloss_range: remaining, enduring, lasting, persisting, and in some forms clinging; locally positive abiding permanence

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the containment and forever phrase that completes the abiding state

words.prose: {{ar:خَٰلِدِينَ}} ({{tr:khālidīna}}) shifts from the landscape to the inhabitants' state. As an accusative circumstantial active participle, it makes permanence the manner in which they are in the gardens, not a separate later promise. The nearby {{ar:فِيهَآ أَبَدًۭا}} ({{tr:fīhā abadan}}) layers containment and unbounded duration onto that state, and the long vowels stretch the duration phrase audibly. The same eternity axis contrasts the opposite destination in 98:6, while the earthly-clinging Form IV remains a contrastive family background rather than the local sense.

topics.headline: abiding is the inhabitants' state
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees eternity as a standing identity and circumstance of the rewarded people.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the active participle a circumstantial accusative describing the people denoted by the opening suffix.

topics.headline: state, interior, and forever converge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices permanence doubled as identity, location, and explicit forever-duration.
topics.reason: {{ar:خَٰلِدِينَ}} ({{tr:khālidīna}}) is followed by the containment phrase and time adverb that complete the duration expression.

topics.headline: positive abiding contrasts fire and earthly clinging
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the same permanence axis split between opposite destinies, while the earthly-clinging form remains a contrastive family background rather than the local sense.
topics.reason: The local active participle selects positive abiding; Form IV clinging is a contrastive root-family pressure, and 98:6 supplies the local opposite destination.

topics.headline: long sounds stretch the duration phrase
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the duration phrase stretch as the scene moves from landscape to abiding people.
topics.reason: The sound row is anchored in the local phrase and the structural row marks the shift from place to inhabitant-state.

words.gloss_range: in them, containment inside the gardens through a feminine suffix referring back to the garden reward

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the earlier garden-suffix phrase that marks the underside source

words.prose: {{ar:فِيهَآ}} ({{tr:fīhā}}) makes the abiding spatially interior: they remain inside the gardens, not merely near them or under their sign. The suffix repeats the garden referent from {{ar:تَحْتِهَا}} ({{tr:taḥtihā}}), so the same gardens are first the source-surface of rivers and then the inhabited interior of the rewarded people.

topics.headline: containment turns permanence into residence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that eternity is placed inside the gardens, not left as abstract duration.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the prepositional phrase complete {{ar:خَٰلِدِينَ}} ({{tr:khālidīna}}) and refer back to the gardens.

topics.headline: same garden pronoun links underside and interior
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees one garden referent carry both river emergence and human residence.
topics.reason: The suffix repeats the garden antecedent already used in {{ar:تَحْتِهَا}} ({{tr:taḥtihā}}).

words.gloss_range: forever, an accusative time adverb giving unbounded duration to the abiding state
words.root_gloss_range: perpetuity, endless futurity, and duration without endpoint; locally an adverbial intensifier of abiding

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the abiding participle modified by the forever adverb
the earlier permanence-bearing Edenic qualifier

words.prose: {{ar:أَبَدًۭا}} ({{tr:abadan}}) seals the material reward beat with a time span that has no boundary. Grammatically it modifies {{ar:خَٰلِدِينَ}} ({{tr:khālidīna}}), so the ayah layers the participial state of abiding with an explicit forever-adverb. Its tanwīn also answers the earlier {{ar:عَدْنٍۢ}} ({{tr:ʿadnin}}), making permanence audible at both the abode and duration points.

topics.headline: forever measures the abiding state
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees forever as a grammatical span applied to the inhabitants' abiding state.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence make {{ar:أَبَدًۭا}} ({{tr:abadan}}) an accusative time adverb intensifying {{ar:خَٰلِدِينَ}} ({{tr:khālidīna}}).

topics.headline: abiding plus forever doubles permanence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices permanence reinforced twice: as an ongoing state and as explicit unbounded duration.
topics.reason: The co-occurrence and local syntax both tie the forever word directly to the abiding participle and paradise formula.

topics.headline: forever closes the paradise scene
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the garden-river-residence beat close on limitless duration before the ayah turns to mutual satisfaction.
topics.reason: The indefinite form and its position after the spatial reward scene make the time limit precisely a no-limit.

words.gloss_range: God was pleased or approved, a perfect Form I verb opening the relational reward beat
words.root_gloss_range: pleasure, satisfaction, approval, acceptance, and being pleased; locally divine approval directed through an ʿan-frame
words.prose: {{ar:رَّضِىَ}} ({{tr:raḍiya}}) moves the ayah from material reward to relational acceptance. The perfect form casts the eschatological approval as settled, and the verb means approval or acceptance, not only an emotion. Because the local form is non-causative, the focus stays on God's approval itself rather than on what causes it. It also begins the reciprocal pattern: God approves them, then they are pleased with Him. The perfect declaration can sound blessing-like, and the reward formulas of 9:72 and 3:15 make this approval beat weighty after the gardens, while 98:6 lacks any matching reciprocity.

topics.headline: perfect verb makes approval settled
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears divine approval as a settled acceptance, not a vague future mood.
topics.reason: QAC marks a perfect Form I verb with {{ar:ٱللَّهُ}} ({{tr:Allāhu}}) as subject, and the lexical field supports approval and acceptance.

topics.headline: approval follows the material paradise beat
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the reward climax move beyond place and duration into divine acceptance.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows cite reward contexts where approval is paired with gardens, including 9:72 and 3:15, and the local verb follows the garden-duration beat.

topics.headline: first approval verb starts reciprocal reversal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that divine approval has priority and then receives a mirrored human response.
topics.reason: The first clause has God as subject and the believers as target; the coordinated second clause reverses subject and target with the same prepositional frame.

topics.headline: approval sounds formulaic and contrasts the prior fate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can hear the approval clause as a compact blessing-like declaration that contrasts 98:6's non-reciprocal fate.
topics.reason: The row's performative overtone is compatible with a perfect declaration, and the sound echo with {{ar:رَضُوا۟}} ({{tr:raḍū}}) helps mark the reciprocal contrast.

topics.headline: Form I keeps God as approving subject
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the clause focus on God's approval itself rather than on something causing God to be pleased.
topics.reason: The local surface is Form I, not the causative form supplied elsewhere in the family.

words.gloss_range: the proper divine name as explicit nominative subject of the approval verb
words.root_gloss_range: divinity, worship, seeking refuge, and disputed derivational fields around the divine name; locally the proper name is selected

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the Lord title that frames the ayah around the proper divine name

words.prose: {{ar:ٱللَّهُ}} ({{tr:Allāhu}}) is the explicit subject of the approval verb, placing the proper divine name at the relational climax of the ayah. The ayah is framed by the title {{ar:رَبّ}} ({{tr:rabb}}), but here the proper name identifies the actor of approval. The name also returns from the command frame of 98:5 into reward approval, with its doubled lām giving the subject acoustic weight. Derivational discussions around worship, refuge, or bewilderment may enrich the name's background, while local grammar keeps it as the unique proper divine subject.

topics.headline: proper name fixes the approving subject
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the approval grounded in the explicit divine name, not inferred only from the Lord frame.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes {{ar:ٱللَّهُ}} ({{tr:Allāhu}}) the nominative subject of {{ar:رَّضِىَ}} ({{tr:raḍiya}}).

topics.headline: derivational dispute enriches without displacing the proper name
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can retain worship/refuge/bewilderment pressure around the divine name while not turning the proper name into a local common noun.
topics.reason: The derivational field is valid background, but QAC marks the local word as a proper noun.

topics.headline: divine name returns from command to approval
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the divine name return from the command frame of 98:5 into the reward-approval scene.
topics.reason: The occurrence row ties the proper name in this ayah to earlier surah command language, and the sound row is anchored in the local surface.

words.gloss_range: with respect to them, the selected prepositional target of divine approval with a plural suffix

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the mirrored singular target phrase in the human satisfaction clause

words.prose: {{ar:عَنْهُمْ}} ({{tr:ʿanhum}}) completes the divine approval frame by marking the believers as the ones with whom God is pleased. The plural suffix keeps the established 98:7 group in view without renaming them. It is also the first half of the prepositional mirror: {{ar:عَنْهُمْ}} ({{tr:ʿanhum}}) will be answered by {{ar:عَنْهُ}} ({{tr:ʿanhu}}), turning divine approval of them into their satisfaction with Him.

topics.headline: selected preposition marks the approval target
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that approval is directed through the verb's selected prepositional frame toward the already established group.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the suffix governed by {{ar:عَنْ}} ({{tr:ʿan}}) as complement of {{ar:رَّضِىَ}} ({{tr:raḍiya}}).

topics.headline: plural target sets up the reciprocal mirror
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the first direction of the approval relation before the second clause reverses it.
topics.reason: The paired {{ar:عَنْ}} ({{tr:ʿan}}) phrases repeat the preposition and change only the target pronoun.

words.gloss_range: coordinating conjunction joining the divine and human satisfaction clauses
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) is the hinge that keeps the second satisfaction clause from sounding like an afterthought. It coordinates two complete clauses: God is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him. Because it sits between repeated satisfaction verbs, the conjunction turns echo into sequence and binds the two directions as one reciprocal claim.

topics.headline: conjunction binds two satisfaction clauses
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees divine approval and human satisfaction as paired halves of one relational statement.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence identifies the second verbal clause as coordinated with the first.

topics.headline: waw mediates the repeated verb echo
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can hear the conjunction as the pivot between two near-repeated approval sounds.
topics.reason: The conjunction is located between the two repeated satisfaction verbs and therefore mediates the echo.

words.gloss_range: they were pleased or satisfied, perfect plural Form I completing the human side of reciprocal satisfaction
words.root_gloss_range: pleasure, satisfaction, acceptance, and approval, with weak-root variation across analyses; locally human satisfaction directed back to God

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the matched divine approval verb in the first reciprocal clause
the weak-root analysis attached to the first approval verb

words.prose: {{ar:رَضُوا۟}} ({{tr:raḍū}}) completes the reciprocal approval pattern. Its implied plural subject is the believers carried from 98:7 through the pronoun chain, and its perfect aspect matches {{ar:رَّضِىَ}} ({{tr:raḍiya}}), making human satisfaction as settled in expression as divine approval. The weak-root variation between {{ar:ر ض و}} ({{tr:r-ḍ-w}}) and {{ar:ر ض ي}} ({{tr:r-ḍ-y}}) does not split the verb family; it lets the near-identical sound support the role reversal, and the same mutual-satisfaction reward formula is attested at 9:100 and 5:119.

topics.headline: perfect plural matches divine approval
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees human satisfaction as a settled reciprocal response, not a loose emotional aside.
topics.reason: The verb is perfect plural and coordinated with the prior perfect singular divine approval verb.

topics.headline: dropped subject resolves to the prior believers
topics.reader_payoff: The reader tracks the unstated human subject back through the ayah's pronoun chain to the believers of 98:7.
topics.reason: The plural verb has no overt subject, and the referent profiles recover the established believing group.

topics.headline: role reversal completes mutual satisfaction
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the subject-object reversal: God to them, then they to Him.
topics.reason: The repeated verb and matching {{ar:عَنْ}} ({{tr:ʿan}}) phrases create a mirrored reciprocal structure.

topics.headline: weak-root variants sound alike while direction changes
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears near-identical satisfaction language across the two directions, while the variant root labels remain analysis-level rather than two separate local meanings.
topics.reason: MASAQ lists weak-root variants for the two forms, and the co-occurrence evidence places mutual satisfaction in reward contexts such as 9:100 and 5:119.

words.gloss_range: with respect to Him, the mirrored prepositional target of human satisfaction

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the plural target phrase mirrored by the singular target phrase
the explicit divine subject referred to by the suffix

words.prose: {{ar:عَنْهُ}} ({{tr:ʿanhu}}) completes the mirror opened by {{ar:عَنْهُمْ}} ({{tr:ʿanhum}}). The same preposition is retained, but the suffix changes to singular, pointing back to {{ar:ٱللَّهُ}} ({{tr:Allāhu}}). That compact pronoun reversal makes the second half of the relation explicit: their satisfaction is directed toward Him.

topics.headline: same preposition reverses the satisfaction target
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the same satisfaction frame turn from God-toward-them to them-toward-God.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes {{ar:عَنْهُ}} ({{tr:ʿanhu}}) the complement of {{ar:رَضُوا۟}} ({{tr:raḍū}}), matching the prior {{ar:عَنْهُمْ}} ({{tr:ʿanhum}}) frame.

topics.headline: singular suffix points back to God
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that a single suffix anchors the human satisfaction back to the explicit divine subject.
topics.reason: The suffix resolves to {{ar:ٱللَّهُ}} ({{tr:Allāhu}}), completing the pronoun-reversal echo.

words.gloss_range: that, a distal demonstrative subject summarizing the entire reward package before assigning it

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the assignment-and-recipient phrase that follows the demonstrative

words.prose: {{ar:ذَٰلِكَ}} ({{tr:dhālika}}) starts a new nominal sentence by gathering the whole reward scene into a single demonstrative: gardens, rivers, permanence, and mutual satisfaction become 'that.' Its distal force gives closure and elevation to what has just been described, while its definiteness prepares the package to be assigned by {{ar:لِمَنْ}} ({{tr:li-man}}) to the one who meets the final condition.

topics.headline: demonstrative gathers the whole reward scene
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the preceding multi-beat reward made into one referent before the final qualification.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence make {{ar:ذَٰلِكَ}} ({{tr:dhālika}}) the subject of a new nominal sentence referring back to the reward package.

topics.headline: distal definiteness prepares restricted assignment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the reward elevated and then restricted to the qualified recipient, not left as a general scene.
topics.reason: The demonstrative is definite and distal, and the following predicate {{ar:لِمَنْ خَشِىَ رَبَّهُۥ}} ({{tr:li-man khashiya rabbahu}}) assigns the summarized package.

words.gloss_range: designation or beneficiary preposition assigning the summarized reward to its qualified recipient

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the relative recipient pronoun attached to the assignment particle
the fused assignment-and-recipient surface unit

words.prose: {{ar:لِ}} ({{tr:li}}) turns the summarized 'that' into an allocation. Attached directly to {{ar:مَنْ}} ({{tr:man}}), it compresses designation and recipient into {{ar:لِمَنْ}} ({{tr:li-man}}): the whole reward package is for, and in that sense belongs to, the one identified by the fear-of-Lord clause.

topics.headline: lam assigns the whole package to its recipient
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the full preceding reward package designated for a defined eligible recipient.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes {{ar:لِمَنْ خَشِىَ رَبَّهُۥ}} ({{tr:li-man khashiya rabbahu}}) the predicate assigning {{ar:ذَٰلِكَ}} ({{tr:dhālika}}).

topics.headline: proclitic fuses assignment to qualification
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the pivot from reward summary to qualifying clause compressed into one surface unit.
topics.reason: The particle is written as a proclitic on {{ar:مَنْ}} ({{tr:man}}), forming the hinge between summary and qualification.

words.gloss_range: whoever or the one who, relative pronoun opening the final qualifying clause

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the assignment particle governing the relative pronoun

words.prose: {{ar:مَنْ}} ({{tr:man}}) opens the final qualifier: the reward belongs to the one who feared his Lord. The local attachment treats it as the object of {{ar:لِ}} ({{tr:li}}) and the head of the relative clause, but the conditional flavor remains meaningful: it identifies the prior believers and also opens the criterion outward as whoever fits it. After plural pronouns have carried the group through the ayah, this singular form individualizes the condition.

topics.headline: relative pronoun supplies the reward recipient
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the ayah turn from describing the reward to naming who it is for.
topics.reason: QAC marks {{ar:مَنْ}} ({{tr:man}}) as a relative pronoun, and attachment evidence makes the following verb phrase its relative clause.

topics.headline: relative and conditional force both matter
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can read the close both backward as identifying the believers and outward as stating general eligibility.
topics.reason: Local grammar supplies a relative parse, while the CRITICAL rows preserve the conditional force as a consequential reading of the same surface.

topics.headline: plural group narrows to individual criterion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the closing condition become personal after a plural reward chain.
topics.reason: The singular form follows a chain of plural suffixes tied to the prior group.

words.gloss_range: feared with reverent, knowledge-shaped awe, a perfect Form I verb supplying the reward condition
words.root_gloss_range: fear, awe, reverent apprehension, and knowledge-shaped recognition of greatness; locally direct fear/awe before one's Lord

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the direct object of the reverent-awe verb

words.prose: {{ar:خَشِىَ}} ({{tr:khashiya}}) supplies the final qualifying action for the whole reward package. The perfect form presents the condition as an achieved posture, while the lexical field points to reverent, knowledge-shaped awe rather than raw fear; the fear-knowledge formula of 35:28 is the clearest supplied parallel. The basic Form I keeps the condition direct rather than reflexive or intensified, and its guttural-sibilant texture makes the close feel hushed and inward. In 98:8 that awe is not abstract, because it takes {{ar:رَبَّهُۥ}} ({{tr:rabbahu}}) as its object and inwardly answers the worship-and-sincere-devotion command structure of 98:5.

topics.headline: perfect verb states achieved qualification
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the closing condition as a completed posture qualifying the whole reward package.
topics.reason: QAC marks {{ar:خَشِىَ}} ({{tr:khashiya}}) as a perfect verb in the relative clause headed by {{ar:مَنْ}} ({{tr:man}}).

topics.headline: khashya is reverent knowledge-shaped awe
topics.reader_payoff: The reader distinguishes informed reverence from generic terror as the qualifying disposition.
topics.reason: The knowledge-based fear claim survives as lexical pressure and is supported by the supplied parallel at 35:28, while the local verb remains direct Form I.

topics.headline: awe is directed to the Lord and closes the surah inwardly
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the final criterion as an inward Lord-directed disposition that corresponds to the outward command structure in 98:5.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes {{ar:رَبَّهُۥ}} ({{tr:rabbahu}}) the direct object, and the CRITICAL rows connect the close to 98:5.

topics.headline: basic form keeps the awe direct
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears a direct, hushed awe verb rather than a reflexive or intensified derivative.
topics.reason: The local verb is Form I, with collocation evidence for the Lord relation and a sound observation tied to the actual surface.

words.gloss_range: his Lord, the singular possessed direct object of the final awe condition
words.root_gloss_range: lordship, ownership, nurturing, sustaining, governing, and mastership; locally personal Lord relation as object of awe

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the reverent-awe verb that takes the Lord phrase as object
the singular qualifying pronoun matched by the suffix
the opening plural Lord relation that forms the bookend

words.prose: {{ar:رَبَّهُۥ}} ({{tr:rabbahu}}) is the ayah's final word and the direct object of {{ar:خَشِىَ}} ({{tr:khashiya}}), so the closing fear is not free-floating: it stands before his Lord. The singular suffix matches {{ar:مَنْ}} ({{tr:man}}), individualizing a reward that has moved through plural pronouns. It also returns to {{ar:رَبِّهِمْ}} ({{tr:rabbihim}}) near the opening, forming a Lordship bookend: reward is with their Lord, and access is conditioned by fearing his Lord.

topics.headline: his Lord is the object of the final awe
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the closing fear directed personally to the Lord, not left as abstract piety.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes {{ar:رَبَّهُۥ}} ({{tr:rabbahu}}) the accusative object of {{ar:خَشِىَ}} ({{tr:khashiya}}).

topics.headline: singular suffix individualizes the condition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the collective reward chain narrow to each person's relation to his Lord.
topics.reason: The singular suffix matches {{ar:مَنْ}} ({{tr:man}}) after plural suffixes have carried the rewarded group.

topics.headline: lordship frames reward and eligibility
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees lordship enclose the whole promise: opening reward-location and closing eligibility condition belong to the same relation.
topics.reason: {{ar:رَبِّهِمْ}} ({{tr:rabbihim}}) near the opening and {{ar:رَبَّهُۥ}} ({{tr:rabbahu}}) at the close form the root and title frame.

topics.headline: last word seals the promise as qualified
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the surah land not on garden imagery alone but on the personal Lord relation that qualifies access.
topics.reason: The closing phrase converts the reward description into a criterion, and the final positioned word names the Lord relation at that endpoint.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: جزاؤهم، عند ربهم، and the reciprocal رضي الله عنهم ورضوا عنه
baseline_models.mechanism: The focus begins with act-matching recompense but locates it in the recipients' Lord's presence and culminates in reciprocal consent. The gardens are therefore one component of a relationship brought into accepted alignment, not the whole content of the reward.

activation_trace.role: Matching an act with its recompense supplies the act-to-outcome correspondence that opens the model.
Proximity and presence place the recompense with their Lord rather than treating it as a detached asset.
Nurture and completion make the repeated Lord-relation the agency that brings the recipients and their outcome to completion.
Reciprocal satisfaction supplies the two-way acceptance that turns recompense into relational settlement.

changed_reading.before: Their reward is principally a unilateral payment consisting of gardens.
changed_reading.after: Their reward is a Lord-held settlement in which fitting recompense, habitation, divine acceptance, and their answering acceptance form one reciprocal outcome.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: جنات عدن تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها أبدا
baseline_models.mechanism: The garden is a tree-covered, vigorously growing enclosure whose lower level carries opened watercourses and ongoing provision. Lordly nurture and the paired duration terms make it a continuously sustained habitat rather than a static scenic prize.

activation_trace.role: The tree-covered enclosure gives the garden its sheltered spatial form.
Thick vigorous plant growth makes the enclosure productive and living rather than merely decorative.
Ongoing provision turns the grammatical flow into the habitat's continuing supply mechanism.
The literal lower side locates the sustaining movement beneath the inhabited garden.
Opening and widening until flow can pass supplies the channels that keep the garden watered.
Stagewise nurture and completion assign maintenance of this living system to the Lord-relation.
Enduring permanence keeps the supplied habitat from running down or passing away.
Emphatic duration extends the maintained condition without a terminal horizon.

changed_reading.before: The verse displays an everlasting garden landscape.
changed_reading.after: The verse presents a protected, cultivated habitat whose hidden flow, growth, provision, and Lordly maintenance remain continuously operative.

baseline_models.mechanism: The closing qualification can hold knowledge and reverent fear together: apprehension of the Lord's authority and nurture becomes awe, so eligibility is a knowing orientation rather than raw fright.

activation_trace.role: The figurative knowledge branch supplies cognitive apprehension to the closing qualification.
Fear joined with awe converts apprehension into a reverent affective stance.
Lordship and authority identify what is known and revered, anchoring the stance in ربه.

changed_reading.before: The reward belongs to whoever is simply afraid of the Lord.
changed_reading.after: The reward belongs to one whose apprehension of the Lord's authority has become reverent, responsive awe.

context_deltas.mechanism: The opening ayah holds unbinding in suspension until disclosure arrives. Against that release axis, the focus ayah's clinging permanence and presence with the Lord read as a settled attachment reached on the far side of disclosed evidence.

activation_trace.role: Clinging and staying close supply the focus state that the context's unbinding axis recasts as settled attachment.
Presence at the Lord gives that settled attachment a relational location.
Opening what is closed and separating what is entangled supplies the release pole against which focus permanence is reread.
Emergence and disclosure make the bayyina the contextual threshold after which attachment can be evaluated.

structural_cues: 98:1 suspends the negated state of being unbound with حتى until the bayyina arrives.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies suspended unbinding, disclosure, focus clinging, and presence; I infer a movement from unresolved attachment to evidence-sealed belonging. A live alternative is that 98:1 only marks the timing of cessation and has no attachment mechanism for 98:8.

changed_reading.after: Abiding also reads as a definitive, disclosed-evidence-tested attachment in the Lord's presence.

context_deltas.mechanism: Purified written surfaces lead into writings that can establish a binding determination and are described through uprightness. These cues activate the debt-settlement branch of جزاء, making the focus reward readable as execution of a clean, upright record rather than an unannounced favor.

activation_trace.role: Collecting or settling a due gives the focus recompense a dischargeable-account form.
Presence and rank at the Lord locate the settlement at its authoritative source.
The written-sheet image supplies a public, readable carrier for what precedes the focus judgment.
Purity as removal of stain qualifies that carrier as uncontaminated.
Writing that establishes an obligating judgment supplies the record-to-verdict function.
Straightness and equilibrium characterize the recorded determination as upright.

structural_cues: 98:2-3 move from recited purified sheets to the writings contained in them and described as qayyima.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies written carriers, purity, binding inscription, uprightness, and a focus due; I infer that the record is executed as recompense. The live alternative is that the writings regulate conduct but do not function as a judgment record.

changed_reading.before: The gardens arrive as a reward whose adjudicative path is unstated.
changed_reading.after: The gardens and reciprocal approval read as the openly executed settlement of an uncontaminated, upright record.

context_deltas.mechanism: The context places division after the clear disclosure has arrived. That sequence blocks a reduction of خشي to information possessed: its knowledge branch must remain joined to awe, because exposure to clarity can still issue in fragmentation rather than the focus ayah's qualifying response.

activation_trace.role: Knowing as a figurative sense supplies the informational component whose sufficiency the context tests.
Reverent fear supplies the responsive orientation that distinguishes khashya from bare reception of evidence.
Scattering into parts supplies the adverse response that follows disclosure.
Arrival fixes the bayyina as already present before the division occurs.
Disclosure and emergence establish that what arrived was manifest rather than hidden.

structural_cues: 98:4 explicitly orders communal division after the bayyina came to its recipients.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies manifest arrival followed by division and focus khashya's knowledge and awe branches; I infer that awe names a response to knowledge rather than knowledge alone. A live alternative is that خشي remains simple fear and the contextual sequence only distinguishes groups.

changed_reading.before: Whoever knows or recognizes the Lord qualifies for the reward.
changed_reading.after: The qualifier is recognition converted into reverent response; manifest information by itself can precede division and does not satisfy the focus condition.

context_deltas.mechanism: Accounting and valuation cues establish a due, while giving and increase redirect that due toward expansion. Joined to the focus branches of debt settlement and ongoing provision, the reward becomes an account whose closure opens into an inexhaustibly continuing grant.

activation_trace.role: Demanding and settling a debt supplies the closing of an account at the focus.
Continuing provision prevents settlement from becoming a one-time exhausted payment.
Accounting and recompense supply the context's explicit ledger-like frame.
Valuation and appraisal supply a measure by which the due can be assessed.
Giving turns assessed obligation into an outward transfer.
Growth and increase make the transfer productive rather than merely subtractive.

structural_cues: 98:5 coordinates religion, establishing, giving, and increase before 98:8 names the recipients' recompense.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies account, valuation, giving, increase, debt settlement, and continuing provision; I supply the arrow by which a settled due becomes an expanding grant. A live alternative is that the 98:5 terms describe obligations only and do not model the reward's mode of delivery.

changed_reading.before: Recompense closes an account with a finite equivalent.
changed_reading.after: Recompense closes what is due yet opens it into continuing, increasing provision, so settlement does not exhaust the gift.

context_deltas.mechanism: The same abiding construction attaches to fire in 98:6 and gardens in 98:8. Permanence is therefore not independently the reward; it intensifies whatever habitat and relation holds the person, while garden, provision, and reciprocal approval make the focus condition desirable.

activation_trace.role: The tree-covered garden supplies the positive habitat to which focus permanence attaches.
Enduring permanence supplies a duration shared with the opposing contextual outcome.
Acceptance opposed to displeasure gives the focus permanence its positive relational quality.
Kindled fire supplies the opposing habitat in which the same duration construction appears.
Enduring permanence on the fire side proves that duration alone is not a positive value.

structural_cues: 98:6 and 98:8 repeat خالدين فيها across fire and gardens, changing the containing habitat while retaining the duration.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies parallel abiding constructions in opposed habitats; I infer that permanence is a neutral amplifier and that habitat plus relation determine its value. A live alternative is that the repetition only emphasizes equal endlessness without inviting functional decomposition.

changed_reading.before: Eternal duration is itself the central reward.
changed_reading.after: Eternal duration fixes attachment; the reward lies in what one is fixed within and in the reciprocal acceptance that characterizes that condition.

context_deltas.mechanism: The immediate context supplies both the wage of intentional work and generosity or gift under خير. The focus matching-recompense branch supports earned correspondence, while its continuing provision exceeds a closed wage, preserving reward as both fitted return and generous grant.

activation_trace.role: Act-matching recompense supplies the earned-correspondence side of the reward.
Ongoing grant supplies an excess beyond a wage that would be paid and exhausted.
The wage or provision of a worker makes intentional deeds legible in an earned-payment register.
Generosity and gift activate a simultaneous non-wage register for the same focus outcome.

structural_cues: 98:7 places intentional work and خير immediately before 98:8 names recompense and depicts continuing flow.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies work-wage, generosity-gift, matching recompense, and ongoing provision; I let both registers qualify one outcome. A live alternative is that خير is only comparative goodness here and contributes no gift mechanism.

changed_reading.before: The outcome must be classified either as wages earned by deeds or as an unearned gift.
changed_reading.after: The outcome holds both registers: it fittingly answers intentional work yet arrives as a generous provision whose flow is not exhausted by equivalence.

context_deltas.mechanism: Inward security and the removal of estrangement in 98:7 feed directly into the focus ayah's reciprocal satisfaction and settled inward state. Reward can thus be read as repaired relation becoming mutually acceptable and internally at rest.

activation_trace.role: Mutual consent supplies the reciprocal relational endpoint of the repair.
A thought settled in the heart gives the enduring outcome an inward resting dimension.
Security and trust that quiet the heart supply the inward condition leading toward settled satisfaction.
Reconciliation that removes estrangement supplies the relational repair completed by mutual رضا.

structural_cues: 98:7's faith-and-repair sequence immediately precedes 98:8's two-directional رضي ... ورضوا construction.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies quiet trust, reconciliation, mutual consent, and inward settling; I infer a causal movement from repaired orientation to reciprocal rest. A live alternative is that صالحات denotes fitting deeds without activating interpersonal reconciliation.

changed_reading.before: Approval is a verdict added after reward has been delivered.
changed_reading.after: Approval is the completion of a repaired relation: estrangement has yielded to mutual consent, and the beneficiaries' inward state has settled with it.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates the non-dominant ج ز ز target in the split mapping for focus جزاء, not the dominant recompense root. It remains anchored to word 1 and gains visible support from the focus garden's vigorous growth and Lordly nurture. Downstream prose should mark it as a form-distant lexical echo, never as the derivation or primary sense of جزاء.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: جزاؤهم beside جنات and the repeated رب relation

activation_trace.role: Readiness for cutting or harvest supplies a form-distant image of recompense arriving when cultivated growth has matured.
Vigorous intertwined growth gives the harvest echo a concrete focus-domain substrate.
Stagewise nurture and completion provide the developmental path by which growth reaches readiness.

changed_reading.before: Recompense is transferred after the relevant acts are complete.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, recompense resembles a harvest at ripeness: Lordly cultivation reaches completion and its mature yield becomes the garden outcome.

strongest_changes: Because خالدين فيها governs both fire and gardens, permanence becomes a neutral fixing of attachment; garden, provision, and reciprocal رضا determine the focus outcome's positive value.
Because manifest evidence is followed by division, خشي ربه cannot be reduced to possessing knowledge; it is recognition converted into reverent response.
Record, account, wage, gift, and growth cues make جزاء an inspectable settlement while its continuing flow keeps that settlement from collapsing into a finite transaction.
summary.what_was_special: The focus ayah interlocks three mechanisms usually flattened into one reward image: a maintained habitat, an enduring attachment, and a reciprocal Lord-human acceptance. Context separates those mechanisms and shows that duration alone is not value, information alone is not khashya, and equivalence alone does not exhaust the gift.
remaining_uncertainties: The move from purified writings to an executed judgment record is reader-supplied; the packet also permits the writings to function only as conduct-guiding prescriptions.
The continuing-provision branch of ج ر ي productively changes the rivers into a supply mechanism, but literal water flow remains the nearer reading.
The harvest model depends on the non-dominant ج ز ز mapping and must remain an exploratory lexical echo.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Reward as settled account near the Lord.** Evidence: ج ز ي B001 recompense matching an act, B002 sufficing/settling a due; ع ن د B004 proximity/presence; ر ب ب B001 lordship/ownership and B002 nurture/completion; د ي ن in 98:5 B002 reckoning and B003 debt. Structural cue: 98:5’s commanded dīn is answered by جزاؤهم. Assigned role: recompense settles the account, nearness locates it, lordship grounds ownership and care. Abductive move: I infer that the reward is not arbitrary surplus but the fitting settlement of a lived obligation. Reading change: جزاؤهم reads as fulfilled relational accounting “with their Lord.”

2. **The garden is protective concealment converted into life, not denial.** Evidence: ج ن ن B001 concealment, B003 tree-covered garden, B008 protective cover, B011 thick growth; ج ر ي B001 flowing and B006 ongoing provision; ن ه ر B001 river cutting ground and B003 opening/widening; ت ح ت B001 underside. Structural cue: earlier negative coverings include كفر and fire; here cover is garden, shade, and flowing provision. Assigned role: jannah covers as protection/growth, rivers cut open channels beneath, flow sustains permanence. Abductive move: I infer that the same root-world of covering can be redeemed when it shelters life instead of hiding truth. Reading change: the garden is a corrected form of concealment: covered, but not deceptive; hidden, but generative.

3. **Permanence rescued from desolation by mutual satisfaction.** Evidence: خ ل د B001 enduring permanence; ء ب د B001 foreverness but also B003 desolate dwelling and B002 wildness; ر ض و B001 acceptance, B002 abundant approval, B003 mutual consent; خ ش ي B001 reverent fear and B002 knowing. Structural cue: 98:6 also has خالدين فيها, so permanence alone is ambiguous until رضى and رب define it. Assigned role: abad intensifies duration; mutual riḍā makes duration habitable; khashya names the reverent knowledge that led there. Abductive move: I infer that endlessness needs relational acceptance to be bliss rather than mere unending enclosure. Reading change: the final state is not just eternal residence; it is permanence transformed by reciprocal divine-human satisfaction.

4. **Fear completes trust instead of negating it.** Evidence: خ ش ي B001 fear/awe and B002 knowing; ء م ن in 98:7 B001 security/trust; ر ب ب B002 nurture/completion. Structural cue: the final phrase returns from plural reward to the singular “who feared his Lord.” Assigned role: khashya individuates the path into awe before a nurturing owner. Abductive move: I infer that fear here is informed recognition, not panic, because it ends in رضى. Reading change: “for whoever feared his Lord” reads as reverent knowing that matures into secure acceptance.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: No later ayah remains to activate this verse. The internal retrospective surprise is that خلد and أبد are not enough to define reward, because 98:6 already uses خالدين for punishment; only عند ربهم, جنات تجري, and mutual رضى convert permanence into blessing.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Recompense as the realized counterpart of action.** **Lexical evidence:** `جَزَاؤُهُمْ` anchors `ج ز ي` B001, “recompense matching an act,” and B002, “standing in and sufficing.” **Structural cue and role:** 98:7 places trusting assent, intentional work, and sound acts directly before this possessive recompense; 98:3–98:5 have already linked upright writings to maintained practice. B001 supplies correspondence, while B002 lets the resulting environment stand as the adequate external counterpart of the prior acts. **Abductive move:** I infer that the garden-world embodies, rather than merely follows, the actors’ maintained order. **Reading change:** reward becomes action translated into a sufficient lived condition, not an arbitrary prize appended to it.

2. **Nearness to a nurturing Lord frames the entire environment.** **Lexical evidence:** `عِندَ` anchors `ع ن د` B004, “proximity and presence”; both occurrences of `رَبّ` anchor `ر ب ب` B001, lordship, and B002, “repair, nurture, and completion.” **Structural cue and role:** `عِندَ رَبِّهِم` introduces the recompense and `خَشِىَ رَبَّه` closes it, enclosing gardens, flow, duration, and approval within the repeated relation. Proximity is the frame; nurture explains the environment’s growth and completion. **Abductive move:** I infer that the spatial imagery elaborates relational nearness and stage-by-stage completion; the packet supplies enclosure but does not rank relation above landscape. **Reading change:** the central reward is presence with the one who has brought formation to completion, with the gardens as its cultivated expression.

3. **Concealment transformed from obstruction into shelter.** **Lexical evidence:** `جَنَّٰت` anchors `ج ن ن` B003, “tree-covered garden,” and activates B001, “covering and concealment.” **Structural cue and role:** within the clipped window, 98:6 has paired truth-covering (`ك ف ر` B001 and B003) with fire; here covering reappears as living canopy over running water. The same material operation, concealment, changes value according to whether it blocks clarity or protects life. **Abductive move:** I infer a deliberate reversal between epistemic cover and arboreal cover from branch resonance; no explicit comparison is stated. **Reading change:** the gardens are not generic scenery but redeemed concealment: a cover that shelters without hiding the truth.

4. **Hidden flow as the infrastructure of continuing provision.** **Lexical evidence:** `تَجْرِى` anchors `ج ر ي` B001, running flow, and activates B006, “ongoing provision or grant”; `تَحْت` anchors `ت ح ت` B001, the lower side; `ٱلْأَنْهَار` anchors `ن ه ر` B001, channels cutting ground, and B003, opening and widening until flow occurs. **Structural cue and role:** water is located beneath the gardens, so an unseen lower channel continuously supports the visible canopy; this follows 98:5’s giving-growth mechanism. **Abductive move:** I infer ecological support and continuous provision from the underflow; the packet gives spatial arrangement and flow, not a botanical causal statement. **Reading change:** the rivers become durable support infrastructure, making reward a self-renewing economy rather than a static possession.

5. **Permanence intensifies attachment but does not determine its value.** **Lexical evidence:** `خَٰلِدِينَ` anchors `خ ل د` B001, permanence, and B002, clinging; `أَبَدًا` anchors `ء ب د` B001, enduring duration, and B006, staying without leaving. **Structural cue and role:** 98:6 and 98:8 share `خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَا`, but only the latter adds `أَبَدًا` and surrounds duration with flow and mutual approval. The repeated frame makes duration morally neutral until its object and relation are specified. **Abductive move:** I infer that prior orientation determines what one becomes attached to; the packet presents parallel outcomes but does not formulate that rule. **Reading change:** eternity is not the whole reward. Its value lies in permanent adhesion to a life-bearing, approved relation rather than to the exposing fire.

6. **Approval as a mirrored, two-way relation.** **Lexical evidence:** both verbs `رَّضِىَ` and `رَضُوا` anchor `ر ض و` B001, acceptance opposed to displeasure, and activate B003, “mutual consent and reciprocal satisfaction.” **Structural cue and role:** the syntax reverses subject and object across the same preposition: God toward them, then they toward Him. That mirror gives the reciprocal branch a visible grammatical mechanism. **Abductive move:** I infer settled relational alignment from the syntactic reversal; reciprocity does not imply equality of parties. **Reading change:** approval is not only a verdict delivered from one side but an achieved correspondence in which divine acceptance and human contentment answer one another.

7. **Awe informed by recognition of nurture.** **Lexical evidence:** `خَشِىَ` anchors `خ ش ي` B001, “fear, dread, and reverent awe,” and activates B002, “knowing as a figurative use”; `رَبَّه` anchors `ر ب ب` B002, nurture and completion. **Structural cue and role:** the final condition comes after clear writings, command, contrasting responses, and their outcomes, and it names the Lord rather than the fire. Knowledge supplies informed recognition; awe supplies the affective force that turns recognition into responsive conduct. **Abductive move:** I infer that disclosed knowledge generates reverent responsiveness to nurture; the form itself can carry awe without asserting the figurative branch. **Reading change:** `خَشِىَ رَبَّه` is not panic before punishment but knowledgeable awe before sustaining authority, the inward orientation from which the preceding practices cohere.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: No later ayah exists in the clipped 98:3–98:8 focus window, so no later-ayah surprise emerged. The section’s surprises are retrospective relations to earlier ayat—especially the shared permanence frame in 98:6, the intentional work in 98:7, and the giving-growth mechanism in 98:5—not activations caused by a subsequent ayah.

baseline.text: Rableri katındaki karşılıkları, altlarından ırmaklar akan Adn bahçeleridir; orada sonsuza dek kalacaklardır. Allah onlardan hoşnut olmuştur, onlar da O'ndan hoşnut olmuşlardır. Bu, Rabbinden korkan kimse içindir.

findings.text: Karşılık, önceki amaçlı davranışların ardından eklenen keyfî bir ödül değil, onların yeterli ve yaşanır bir duruma dönüşmüş uygun sonucudur.
Rablerinin katında oluş, bütün bahçe, süre ve hoşnutluk tasvirini yetiştiren ve tamamlayan Rabbe yakınlık ilişkisi içine yerleştirir.
Bahçenin örtüsü, gerçeği gizleyen örtmenin tersine, hayatı saklamadan koruyan ve büyüten bir sığınağa dönüşür.
Bahçelerin altındaki akış, görünen hayatı alttan sürekli besleyen, kanallar açarak kendini yenileyen bir destek düzeni oluşturur.
Sonsuzluk tek başına ödülün değerini belirlemez; değer, hayat veren ve onaylanmış bir ilişkiye ayrılmadan bağlanmaktan gelir.
Rabden korkmak, cezadan duyulan panikten öte, yetiştiren otoriteyi tanıyan bilgili ve karşılık veren bir saygıdır.
Karşılıklı hoşnutluk, kendi başına ıssız ve çıkışsız bir süre olabilecek ebediliği yaşanabilir kılan unsur olarak yorumlanabilir.

butuncul_okuma_line.raw_line: **98:8.** جَزَآؤُهُمْ عِندَ رَبِّهِمْ جَنَّٰتُ عَدْنٍۢ تَجْرِى مِن تَحْتِهَا ٱلْأَنْهَٰرُ خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَآ أَبَدًۭا ۖ رَّضِىَ ٱللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ وَرَضُوا۟ عَنْهُ ۚ ذَٰلِكَ لِمَنْ خَشِىَ رَبَّهُۥ — Birincil okuma: Onların karşılığı Rablerinin yanında, altlarından ırmaklar akan adn cennetleri ve ebedî kalıştır. 98:6’da da kalıcılık bulunduğu için sürpriz, ebediliğin tek başına ödül olmaması; onu nimet yapan şeyin Rab yakınlığı, hayat veren akış, koruyucu örtü ve Allah ile kullar arasındaki karşılıklı rıza olmasıdır. {ج ز ي B001; ج ز ي B002; ع ن د B004; ر ب ب B001; ر ب ب B002; ج ن ن B003; ج ن ن B008; ج ر ي B001; ج ر ي B006; ن ه ر B001; ن ه ر B003; خ ل د B001; ء ب د B001; ر ض و B001; ر ض و B003; خ ش ي B001; خ ش ي B002}

butuncul_okuma_line.reading_text_tr: Onların karşılığı Rablerinin yanında, altlarından ırmaklar akan adn cennetleri ve ebedî kalıştır. 98:6’da da kalıcılık bulunduğu için sürpriz, ebediliğin tek başına ödül olmaması; onu nimet yapan şeyin Rab yakınlığı, hayat veren akış, koruyucu örtü ve Allah ile kullar arasındaki karşılıklı rıza olmasıdır.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: A person is directed, straightened, and cleansed for undivided service.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Worship is directed to one deity through obedience and an allotment withheld from partners.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: The central act is exclusive direction: service and دين are assigned without a partner. The latent image of bodily lowering intensifies this orientation, while partnership marks the precise relation being refused.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: A person is directed, straightened, and cleansed for undivided service.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Naming opens the address, lordship identifies the addressee, supplication carries the request, and amen supplies the answering assent. The result is a compact call-and-response ritual.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Conviction and Learned Discernment

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Inner judgment settles into belief, guarded fear, evaluation, or contentment.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Grinding prepares the aromatic base, smoke or mineral supplies pigment, and lime alters body hair. Mustache fullness gives the grooming scene its bodily target, while purification governs preparation and application.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Ambush, Snare, and Lure
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A hunter hides in a blind, lures prey from shelter, and catches it in a snare or trap.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: snare `ش ر ك:B006/m01`; trap `ص ل و:B004/m01`; hunter's blind `ب ر ء:B007/m01`; concealed refuge `ج ن ن:B017/m01`; luring an animal from its burrow `خ ي ر:B006/m01`; sudden snatch `ن ه ر:B006/m01`
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Concealment protects the hunter, lure initiates movement, and trap converts that movement into capture. The snatch is the abrupt terminal action of the same tactical sequence.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Small Prey, Serpent, and Blindness

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: serpent `ج ن ن:B012/m01`; blind burrowing rodent `خ ل د:B005/m01`; gnat-like irritant `ش ر ر:B009/m01`; lure from a burrow `خ ي ر:B006/m01`; intact-looking blind eye `ق و م:B021/m01`
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Burrow and concealment define the habitat, serpent and irritant define danger, and blindness complicates pursuit or perception. The intact eye with lost sight gives a bodily analogue to the unseen movement underground.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Rivalry, Wrestling, and Overcoming
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Matched opponents engage, resist, and seek to overcome one another.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: overcoming in reciprocal action `ج ز ي:B005/m01`; resistance and wrestling `ق و م:B014/m01`; matching competition `ج ر ي:B007/m01`; victory in a satisfaction contest `ر ض و:B005/m01`; victory in contest `ر ض ي:B002/m01`
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Matching creates comparable opponents, resistance sustains the encounter, and overcoming produces an asymmetric result. The satisfaction branches preserve the interpersonal setting by describing victory over another claimant.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Coercion and Rebellion
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Pressure forces a subject toward disobedience, and the subject may harden into opposition.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: compulsion `ج ي ء:B005/m01`; coercion into disobedience `ك ف ر:B007/m01`; obstinate opposition `ع ن د:B001/m01`; enmity `ب ع د:B010/m01`
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Compulsion applies force, coerced disobedience redirects conduct, and obstinacy makes resistance durable. Enmity is the social state that remains after pressure and rebellion polarize the parties.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Deliberation reaches penetrating judgment, total self-commitment, weak-minded compliance, futility, anger, and rebuke.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Futility, No Choice, and Strain
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Effort continues after useful options have closed and produces strain without benefit.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: lack of utility `ب ع د:B009/m01`; no way or choice `ع ن د:B005/m01`; exertion and trouble `ع م ل:B007/m01`; adverse condition `ك و ن:B006/m01`
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: No-choice closes the decision space, futility removes expected gain, and effort becomes pure strain. The adverse condition is therefore both the cause and outcome of ineffective action.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Anger, Regret, and Harsh Rebuke
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A grave affair provokes anger, hardens into verbal rebuke, and may end in regret after loss.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: anger `ء ب د:B009/m01`; anger and offended pride `ع ب د:B008/m01`; regret after loss `ع ب د:B008/m02`; harsh rebuke `ن ه ر:B004/m01`; grave or monstrous affair `ء م ر:B006/m01`
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: The affair supplies the provocation, anger supplies the immediate state, and rebuke externalizes it in speech. Regret appears when the object of anger or effort is already lost.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Labor Crew, Wage, and Stipend
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A crew performs assigned labor and receives recurring support for its livelihood.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: manual workers `ع م ل:B006/m01`; wage `ع م ل:B004/m01`; stipend `ج ر ي:B006/m01`; livelihood `ق و م:B009/m01`; enrolled service `ك ت ب:B004/m01`
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: The crew supplies collective agency, enrollment fixes obligation, and wage or stipend sustains continued service. Livelihood is the stable outcome of repeated compensated work.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Willing Gift and Welfare
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A giver voluntarily presents a benefit in response to another's need.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: giving and bestowal `ء ت ي:B002/m01`; willing transfer `ر س ل:B010/m01`; generous gift `خ ي ر:B005/m01`; need `ر ب ب:B016/m01`; blessing and benefaction `ر ب ب:B016/m03`
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Need supplies the receiving condition, willing transfer preserves the giver's agency, and gift supplies the concrete benefit. Blessing names the surplus value by which the transfer becomes welfare rather than bare exchange.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Concealed Beings
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Unseen beings inhabit a concealed or densely hidden place.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: jinn as concealed beings `ج ن ن:B005/m01`; concealment `ج ن ن:B001/m01`; hidden place `ج ن ن:B017/m01`; densely enclosed garden `ج ن ن:B003/m01`
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: The same root organizes agent, setting, and operation: beings are hidden, their place conceals them, and enclosure gives the habitat density. Garden and jinn meet through the invariant of screened interiority.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Concealed Thought and Derangement
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A thought settles inside the heart, remains inaccessible to others, or loses coherence when the mind is covered.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: hidden heart and thought `ج ن ن:B010/m01`; thought lodged within `خ ل د:B004/m01`; madness as covering of reason `ج ن ن:B006/m01`; weak testimony `ب ي ن:B011/m03`
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Lodged thought describes durable interior content, while madness describes the loss of access to ordered reason. Weak testimony is the discourse consequence when an inward state cannot be made reliably clear.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak sözü, yapılan bir iyiliğe iyilikle, kötülüğe de kötülükle karşılık vermeyi açıkça ortak çekirdek olarak gösterir. Ödül, olumsuz yaptırım ve öç alma bu iki yönlü karşılık ilişkisinin özel görünümleridir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal yalnızca olumlu bir ödülü ya da yalnızca olumsuz bir yaptırımı anlatmaz; karşılığın iki yönünü de kapsar.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım, genel karşılık verme çekirdeğini korurken belirli kalıplara bağlı hızlı öç alma ve hak edilmiş karşılık kullanımlarını ayrı, bağımlı görünümler olarak tutar.

concept_map.definition: Bir kişinin yaptığına, iyiyse iyilikle ve kötüyse kötülükle, ona denk ve yeterli bir karşılık vermektir. Ödüllendirme, olumsuz yaptırım ve öç alma bu çekirdeğin yön ya da kullanım bakımından özelleşmiş görünümleridir.

facets.statement: Yapılan eylem, niteliğine uygun ve onu karşılayacak bir iyilik ya da kötülükle yanıtlanır.
Olumlu yönde ödül, olumsuz yönde ise yaptırım ya da öç biçiminde gerçekleşebilir.
Hızlı öç almayı ve övgüye değer işlerle yerine getirilmesi gereken yükümlülüklerin karşılıklarını anlatan özel kullanımlar da bu çekirdeğe bağlıdır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynakların ortak çizgisi, karşılığın yapılan işe denk düşmesi ve hem iyi hem kötü yönde olabilmesidir; ödül ile yaptırım bu ortak yapının karşıt yönleridir.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak sözü, bir şeyin ya da kişinin başkasının yerini tutmasını, onun adına işi görmesini ve yeterli olmasını ortak çekirdek olarak verir. İş görme, bir borcu ödeme ve bir edimin sahibi adına yeterli sayılması bu çekirdeğin özel uygulamalarıdır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu dal yapılan işe ödül ya da yaptırım vermeyi değil, başka birinin veya şeyin yerine geçerek yükümlülüğü karşılamayı anlatır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım, yerini tutma ve yeterli olma çekirdeğini genel biçimde verir; kişi, hayvan, iş, borç ve ödeme kalıplarını bu çekirdeğin ayrı uygulamaları olarak sınırlar.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyin ya da kişinin başkasının yerini tutup onun adına bir işi veya yükümlülüğü karşılaması ve yeterli olmasıdır. İş görme, borç ödeme ve bir edimin sahibi adına yeterli sayılması bu çekirdeğin özel gerçekleşimleridir.

facets.statement: Bir şey ya da kişi başka birinin yerini tutar, onun yerine iş görür ve gereksinimi karşılar.
Bir işin, onu yapması gereken kimse adına tamamlanması yerini tutma çekirdeğinin bir uygulamasıdır.
Birinin alacağını veya borcunu ödemek ya da bir edimin sahibi adına yeterli sayılması da aynı çekirdeğe bağlıdır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar, yerini tutma ile yeterli olmayı tek yapıda birleştirir; başka biri adına iş görme, ödeme yapma ve yükümlülüğü karşılama bu yapının uygulamalarıdır.
